thread:
Alex: Quick sync — product wants to flip the implicit server default for /v1/chat to `redwood-3` on 2025-11-15. Before we announce, can we confirm SDK auto-pin behaviour and server fallback semantics? What exactly will break for customers?

Maria: Do we have a formal migration window? 60 days? Need to know so SDKs can decide whether to keep auto-pinning old default.

Alex: Product mentioned 60d deprecation with a 2-week canary. But we need concrete answers from runtime + SDKs: if a client omits `model`, will the server return the new default, an error, or a clear deprecation header?

Sam: Runtime options: 1) keep returning old default for customers with a "pinned" account property, 2) return new default for everyone, or 3) return 400/422 if no model and no client pin. Option 3 is safest to force explicit pin, but will be noisy.

Julia: We prefer 2 (switch to new default) with strong warnings first, but product is worried about subtle regressions for ML-sensitive apps. Can we support a compatibility header during the window?

Alex: Proposal: on 2025-10-15 start sending `Warning: model-default change scheduled 2025-11-15; set Accept-Model to opt-in` in responses for requests without explicit model. Then on the flip date, server honors `Accept-Model: previous` if present, otherwise uses new default. That gives a soft opt-out. Thoughts?

Maria: That seems reasonable. SDKs should surface the warning and optionally auto-add `Accept-Model: previous` for one release so customers don't break unexpectedly. But we must avoid permanently encouraging implicit defaults.

Sam: Implementation notes: we can add a runtime flag `compat-accept-model` that checks header and falls back to the legacy default if header == "previous". We'll gate it behind a rollout flag and metrics. Do we have a telemetry event to track how many requests use the header?

Alex: Add metric `model_default_header_usage` with labels `region` and `client_sdk`. Also emit `x-redwood-deprecation: model-default` header starting 2025-10-15.

Maria: I'll open SDK PRs to: 1) keep local pinning behavior for the next release, 2) surface deprecation warnings in logs, 3) add an opt-in feature to auto-send `Accept-Model: previous` for the 60d window.

Julia: Docs action: publish migration guide with recommended code changes and a checklist for customers. I'll coordinate timing with marketing for the public notice.

docs-bot: docs PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4123 — adds migration guide and header spec. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Example client guidance to include in docs:
```
# Python SDK (recommended explicit model)
resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-3", messages=...)

# Temporary opt-out via header (only during migration window)
resp = client.chat.create(messages=..., headers={"Accept-Model": "previous"})
```

Sam: Edgecases: streaming clients that rely on token distribution/perf might see different latency/cost with redwood-3. We should include perf profiles in the announcement so customers can plan.

Maria: Action items for eng:
- add `x-redwood-deprecation: model-default` header by 2025-10-15 (runtime)
- implement `Accept-Model` runtime toggle and rollout flag by 2025-10-22
- emit `model_default_header_usage` metric by 2025-10-22
- SDK PRs for explicit pin + opt-in header before 2025-10-01

Alex: I'll own the comms and coordinate canary dates with infra. Can we get a short checklist from eng leads by EOD tomorrow?

Julia: Can do. I'm also adding a note to the canary playbook to include automatic rollback if we see >1% increase in error rate or 5% tail latency regression.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: 2025-10-29 05:00 UTC -> us-west1 (5%), eu-central1 (5%). Monitoring hooks enabled.

Maria: I'll send a PR link for the SDK changes once ready. Thanks — this plan looks solid. :thumbsup:
